column2: On the authority of Abū al-ʿAbbās Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: “A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah,

direct me to a deed which, if I do it, Allah will love me and people will love me. He said: Renounce the world and Allah will love you, and renounce what people possess and people will love you.” Reported by Ibn Mājah and others with ḥasan chains.
Dullanī (“direct me”): guide me, “to a deed”: of deeds.
“If I do it”: if I perform it.
“Renounce the world”: limit yourself to the necessary amount of it.
“Renounce what people possess”: of worldly things.
“People will love you”: because you hold back from their worldly goods.
Renouncing the world is among the causes of Allah's love for His servant and of people's love.
There is nothing wrong with striving for what earns a person the love of [Allah's] servants, provided it is not unlawful.
A person should treat people well so that it becomes a cause of his being loved.
A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to guide him to a deed which, if he did it, would be a cause of Allah's loving him and of people's love,
and the Prophet ﷺ guided him to a comprehensive, all-embracing deed that would bring him the love of Allah and the love of people.
He ﷺ said to him: “Renounce the world”,
that is, seek from it only what you need and leave the surplus,
and what does not benefit in the Hereafter, and be scrupulous about anything that may harm your religion; and renounce the worldly things that people deal in.

If some right or contract arises between you and any of them, be as has come in the hadith: “May Allah have mercy on a man who is easy-going when he sells, easy-going when he buys, easy-going when he repays and easy-going when he asks for repayment”, so that you are loved by people and shown mercy by Allah.
Among what has been said on this:
Renounce what the hands of mankind contain, / and you will become beloved to all people.
Another poet:
If you shun it [this world], you are at peace with its people; / but if you try to pull it to you, its dogs will fight you for it.
Another poet:
If this world were a reward for the doer of good, / there would be no living in it for the wrongdoer.
The prophets went hungry in it as an honour, / while the bellies of beasts have eaten their fill in it.
